```
    <!-- Main Content -->
    <main class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto pt-14 lg:pt-0">
      <div class="p-4 sm:p-6 lg:p-8 max-w-7xl mx-auto">

        <!-- Page Loader -->
        <div id="page-loader" class="hidden fixed inset-0 z-20 bg-white/60 flex items-center justify-center">
          <div class="loader"></div>
        </div>

        <!-- Dashboard -->
        <section id="page-dashboard" class="hidden">
          <div class="mb-8">
            <h1 class="text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-bold text-slate-900">Welcome back, <span id="dash-username">User</span></h1>
            <p class="text-slate-500 mt-1">Here's your financial overview</p>
          </div>
          <div class="bg-gradient-to-r from-blue-600 to-blue-700 rounded-2xl p-6 text-white mb-8">
            <p class="text-blue-100 text-sm font-medium">Total Balance</p>
            <p class="text-3xl font-bold mt-1" id="dash-total-balance">$0.00</p>
          </div>
          <h2 class="text-lg font-semibold text-slate-900 mb-4">Your Accounts</h2>
          <div id="dash-accounts" class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-3 gap-4 mb-8"></div>

          <!-- White-Label Insurance Card -->
          <div class="bg-gradient-to-r from-slate-900 via-navy-900 to-navy-800 rounded-2xl p-6 text-white mb-8 border border-navy-700 shadow-sm flex flex-col md:flex-row md:items-center justify-between gap-4">
            <div class="flex items-center gap-4">
              <div class="w-12 h-12 rounded-xl bg-amber-500/20 border border-amber-500/30 flex items-center justify-center flex-shrink-0">
                <svg class="w-6 h-6 text-amber-400" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M9 12l2 2 4-4m5.618-4.016A11.955 11.955 0 0112 2.944a11.955 11.955 0 01-8.618 3.04A12.02 12.02 0 003 9c0 5.591 3.824 10.29 9 11.622 5.176-1.332 9-6.03 9-11.622 0-1.042-.133-2.052-.382-3.016z"></path></svg>
              </div>
              <div>
                <h3 class="font-bold text-lg text-white">FACE Insurance Partner Portal</h3>
                <p class="text-sm text-navy-200 mt-0.5">Manage your motor, home, and contents policies or lodge claims with single sign-on.</p>
              </div>
            </div>
            <button onclick="BankOfEd.App.launchInsurance(event)" class="bg-amber-500 hover:bg-amber-600 text-slate-950 font-semibold px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl transition-colors flex items-center justify-center gap-2 whitespace-nowrap self-start md:self-auto shadow">
              <span>Launch FACE Insurance</span>
              <svg class="w-4 h-4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M10 6H6a2 2 0 00-2 2v10a2 2 0 002 2h10a2 2 0 002-2v-4M14 4h6m0 0v6m0-6L10 14"></path></svg>
            </button>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white rounded-2xl shadow-sm border border-slate-100 overflow-hidden">
            <div class="px-6 py-4 border-b border-slate-100">
              <h2 class="text-lg font-semibold text-slate-900">Recent Activity</h2>
            </div>
            <div id="dash-transactions" class="divide-y divide-slate-100"></div>
            <div id="dash-no-transactions" class="hidden p-8 text-center text-slate-400">No recent transactions</div>
          </div>
        </section>

        <!-- Accounts List -->
        <section id="page-accounts" class="hidden">
          <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-8">
            <div>
              <h1 class="text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-bold text-slate-900">Accounts</h1>
              <p class="text-slate-500 mt-1">Manage your bank accounts</p>
            </div>
            <button onclick="BankOfEd.AccountsPage.showNewAccountModal()" class="bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 text-white font-medium px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl transition-colors flex items-center gap-2">
              <svg class="w-5 h-5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M12 4v16m8-8H4"></path></svg>
              <span class="hidden sm:inline">Open Account</span>
            </button>
          </div>
          <div id="accounts-list" class="space-y-4"></div>
          <div id="accounts-empty" class="hidden bg-white rounded-2xl shadow-sm border border-slate-100 p-12 text-center">
            <svg class="w-16 h-16 text-slate-300 mx-auto mb-4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="1.5" d="M3 10h18M7 15h1m4 0h1m-7 4h12a3 3 0 003-3V8a3 3 0 00-3-3H6a3 3 0 00-3 3v8a3 3 0 003 3z"></path></svg>
            <p class="text-slate-500 text-lg">No accounts yet</p>
            <p class="text-slate-400 mt-1">Open your first account to get started</p>
          </div>
        </section>

        <!-- Account Detail -->
        <section id="page-account-detail" class="hidden">
          <a href="#/accounts" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-blue-600 hover:text-blue-700 text-sm font-medium mb-6">
            <svg class="w-4 h-4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M15 19l-7-7 7-7"></path></svg>
            Back to Accounts
          </a>
          <div id="account-detail-header" class="bg-white rounded-2xl shadow-sm border border-slate-100 p-6 mb-6"></div>
          <div class="bg-white rounded-2xl shadow-sm border border-slate-100 overflow-hidden">
            <div class="px-6 py-4 border-b border-slate-100">
              <h2 class="text-lg font-semibold text-slate-900">Transaction History</h2>
            </div>
            <div id="account-detail-transactions"></div>
            <div id="account-detail-pagination" class="px-6 py-4 border-t border-slate-100 flex items-center justify-between"></div>
          </div>
        </section>

        <!-- Transfers -->
        <section id="page-transfers" class="hidden">
          <div class="mb-8">
            <h1 class="text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-bold text-slate-900">Transfer Money</h1>
            <p class="text-slate-500 mt-1">Send money between accounts or to someone else</p>
          </div>
          <div class="bg-white rounded-2xl shadow-sm border border-slate-100 overflow-hidden">
            <!-- Transfer Tabs -->
            <div class="flex border-b border-slate-200">
              <button id="transfer-tab-own" onclick="BankOfEd.TransfersPage.switchTab('own')" class="flex-1 py-4 text-center font-semibold text-blue-600 border-b-2 border-blue-600 transition-colors">Between Own Accounts</button>
              <button id="transfer-tab-external" onclick="BankOfEd.TransfersPage.switchTab('external')" class="flex-1 py-4 text-center font-semibold text-slate-400 border-b-2 border-transparent hover:text-slate-600 transition-colors">Pay Someone</button>
            </div>

            <!-- Own Transfer -->
            <div id="transfer-own-panel" class="p-6 sm:p-8">
              <form id="transfer-own-form" onsubmit="BankOfEd.TransfersPage.handleOwnTransfer(event)" class="space-y-5 max-w-lg">
                <div>
                  <label class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">From Account</label>
                  <select id="transfer-own-from" required class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition bg-white"></select>
                </div>
                <div>
                  <label class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">To Account</label>
                  <select id="transfer-own-to" required class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition bg-white"></select>
                </div>
                <div>
                  <label id="transfer-own-amount-label" class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">Amount (AUD)</label>
                  <input type="number" id="transfer-own-amount" required step="0.01" min="0.01" class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition" placeholder="0.00" oninput="BankOfEd.TransfersPage.onOwnAmountChange && BankOfEd.TransfersPage.onOwnAmountChange()">
                  <div id="transfer-own-fx-section" class="hidden mt-2">
                    <label class="block text-xs font-medium text-slate-500 mb-1">Currency</label>
                    <select id="transfer-own-amount-currency" class="w-full px-3 py-2 rounded-lg border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-purple-500 focus:border-purple-500 outline-none transition bg-white text-sm"></select>
                    <div id="transfer-own-conversion"></div>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <div>
                  <label class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">Description <span class="text-slate-400">(optional)</span></label>
                  <input type="text" id="transfer-own-desc" maxlength="255" class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition" placeholder="e.g. Monthly savings">
                </div>
                <div id="transfer-own-errors" class="text-sm text-red-600 hidden"></div>
                <button type="submit" class="bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 text-white font-semibold px-8 py-3 rounded-xl transition-colors flex items-center gap-2">
                  <span>Transfer</span>
                  <svg class="w-4 h-4 animate-spin hidden" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle class="opacity-25" cx="12" cy="12" r="10" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="4" fill="none"></circle><path class="opacity-75" fill="currentColor" d="M4 12a8 8 0 018-8V0C5.373 0 0 5.373 0 12h4z"></path></svg>
                </button>
              </form>
            </div>

            <!-- External Transfer -->
            <div id="transfer-external-panel" class="p-6 sm:p-8 hidden">
              <form id="transfer-ext-form" onsubmit="BankOfEd.TransfersPage.handleExternalTransfer(event)" class="space-y-5 max-w-lg">
                <div>
                  <label class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">From Account</label>
                  <select id="transfer-ext-from" required class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition bg-white"></select>
                </div>

                <!-- Payee Method Toggle -->
                <div>
                  <label class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-2">Pay To</label>
                  <div class="flex gap-2">
                    <button type="button" id="ext-method-addressbook" onclick="BankOfEd.TransfersPage.setPayeeMethod('addressbook')" class="flex-1 py-2.5 px-4 rounded-xl border-2 border-blue-600 bg-blue-50 text-blue-700 font-medium text-sm transition-colors">Address Book</button>
                    <button type="button" id="ext-method-manual" onclick="BankOfEd.TransfersPage.setPayeeMethod('manual')" class="flex-1 py-2.5 px-4 rounded-xl border-2 border-slate-200 text-slate-600 font-medium text-sm hover:border-slate-300 transition-colors">Enter Manually</button>
                  </div>
                </div>

                <!-- Address Book Selection -->
                <div id="ext-addressbook-section">
                  <label class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">Select Payee</label>
                  <select id="transfer-ext-payee" class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition bg-white">
                    <option value="">Choose a payee...</option>
                  </select>
                </div>

                <!-- Manual Entry -->
                <div id="ext-manual-section" class="hidden space-y-4">
                  <div>
                    <label class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">BSB</label>
                    <input type="text" id="transfer-ext-bsb" maxlength="7" class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition" placeholder="000-000">
                  </div>
                  <div>
                    <label class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">Account Number</label>
                    <input type="text" id="transfer-ext-account" maxlength="8" class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition" placeholder="12345678">
                  </div>
                  <div>
                    <label class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">Payee Name</label>
                    <input type="text" id="transfer-ext-payee-name" class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition" placeholder="Recipient name">
                  </div>
                </div>

                <div>
                  <label id="transfer-ext-amount-label" class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 mb-1.5">Amount (AUD)</label>
                  <input type="number" id="transfer-ext-amount" required step="0.01" min="0.01" class="w-full px-4 py-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500 outline-none transition" placeholder="0.00" oninput="BankOfEd.TransfersPage.onExtAmountChange && BankOfEd.TransfersPage.onExtAmountChange()">
                  <div id="transfer-ext-fx-section" class="hidden mt-2">
                    <label class="block text-xs font-medium text-slate-500 mb-1">Currency</label>
                    <select id="transfer-ext-amount-currency" class="w-full px-3 py-2 rounded-lg border border-slate-300 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-purple-500 focus:border-purple-500 outline-none transition bg-white text-sm"></select>
                    <div id="transfer-ext-conversion"></div>
                  </div>
```

### Validation Note
I re-requested both /banking/ and the exact /banking/#/accounts URL without the scanner's X-Rewrite-URL header. Both direct Apache responses were 200 and omitted CSP, X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS, and Referrer-Policy; the HTML head also had no equivalent meta policy. This rules out proxy stripping, fragment routing, and meta-tag compensation as innocent explanations.

### Validation Command
```
curl -s -S -i -k -L --max-time 20 'http://localhost:8081/banking/#/accounts'
```

## 54. FX conversion API reflects arbitrary CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-053
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: confirmed
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/fx/convert?from=AUD&to=USD&amount=1
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The authenticated FX conversion endpoint reflects an arbitrary Origin request header in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.

### Impact
An attacker-controlled website may be able to read authenticated API responses in a victim's browser if the browser includes the required credentials. The demonstrated response exposed only FX conversion data.

### Likelihood
Origin reflection was reproduced using an authenticated bearer session. No browser-based proof demonstrated that credentials are sent or that sensitive data can be read cross-origin.

### Recommendation
Allow CORS only for explicitly trusted application origins. For all other Origin values, omit Access-Control-Allow-Origin and other CORS permission headers. Apply the allowlist consistently across authenticated endpoints.

### Evidence
```
An authenticated GET request to /api/fx/convert?from=AUD&to=USD&amount=1 supplied Origin: https://evil.example. The API returned HTTP 200 with FX conversion data and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example.
```

### Request Evidence
```
GET /api/fx/convert?from=AUD&to=USD&amount=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8081
Origin: https://evil.example
Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED_BEARER] admin_active_0912 token]
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"success":true,"data":{"from":"AUD","to":"USD","amount":"1","converted_amount":"0.64","rate":"0.63694267"},"message":"OK"}
```

### Validation Note
Using the valid `admin_fresh` session, I compared a same-origin request with `Origin: https://evil.example`. Both returned the same authenticated FX data, while the server changed `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to exactly match the supplied origin and also returned `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. A separate Authorization preflight for the evil origin returned 200 with permissive CORS headers, so origin validation or preflight rejection does not provide an innocent explanation.

### Validation Command
```
curl -s -S -i -k -L --max-time 20 -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' 'http://localhost:8081/api/fx/convert?from=AUD&to=USD&amount=1' -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat aespa-poc-auth.txt)"
```

### Validation Setup
This finding requires an authenticated session (log in as **admin_fresh** or an equivalent user).

Log in as the admin user and copy the bearer token from the Authorization request header or browser storage.

Capture the credential into a file named `aespa-poc-auth.txt` in the directory you run the command from:

In the browser DevTools Console (adjust the storage key for the app):
```js
const token = localStorage.getItem('token'); // or sessionStorage
const a = document.createElement('a');
a.href = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([token], {type:'text/plain'}));
a.download = 'aespa-poc-auth.txt'; a.click();
```

Then move `aespa-poc-auth.txt` next to where you run the command below.

## 55. Login endpoint does not throttle repeated failed attempts

- Finding reference: KOWT-006
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A07
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: confirmed
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/auth/login
- CVSS: 3.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L)

### Description
The login endpoint accepted six consecutive failed password attempts for a known-valid account without a visible delay, throttling response, CAPTCHA, or temporary account lockout.

### Impact
An attacker could automate password guessing or credential-stuffing attempts against customer accounts.

### Likelihood
The endpoint is remotely accessible without authentication, and the tested sequence encountered no control that would slow repeated attempts. Only six attempts were tested, so behavior over longer attack sequences was not established.

### Recommendation
Apply rate limits per account and source, with progressive delays and monitoring. Temporarily lock accounts or require an additional challenge after repeated failures. When throttling requests, return HTTP 429 with an appropriate Retry-After header.

### Evidence
```
Six consecutive failed login requests returned the same HTTP 401 WRONG_PASSWORD response. Attempt 1 completed in 79 ms, attempts 2 through 5 completed in 71-76 ms, and attempt 6 completed in 70 ms. No Retry-After header or throttling response was observed.
```

### Request Evidence
```
Six consecutive POST /api/auth/login requests for amelia.chen@example.com with password wrong-0912 under bounded sequence amelia-login-rate-limit-0912.
```

### Response Evidence
```
Attempt 1: HTTP 401, 79 ms, WRONG_PASSWORD. Attempt 6: HTTP 401, 70 ms, WRONG_PASSWORD. No Retry-After header or throttling response.
```

### Validation Note
I tested the main innocent explanation, that throttling or lockout starts within a fresh bounded six-attempt window. Six additional cookie-free POST requests for the known account all returned the same 401 WRONG_PASSWORD response in 69-138 ms, with no Retry-After header, CAPTCHA, delay, or lockout response. This independently matches the scanner evidence, so I could not identify a benign rate-limit mechanism that explains the behavior. No single HTTP request can demonstrate the absence of throttling, so a one-request PoC is omitted rather than providing a misleading proof.

## 56. Login responses allow customer email enumeration

- Finding reference: KOWT-007
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A07
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: confirmed
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/auth/login
- CVSS: 3.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The login endpoint returns different error codes and messages depending on whether the submitted email belongs to a registered customer.

### Impact
An unauthenticated attacker could identify registered customer email addresses and use them in targeted phishing, password-guessing, or credential-stuffing attempts.

### Likelihood
Exploitation requires only repeated login requests and comparison of the responses. The observed differences reliably distinguish a known email from an unknown email.

### Recommendation
Return the same HTTP status, response body, and error code for all authentication failures, such as "Invalid email or password." Keep processing times similar to reduce timing-based enumeration.

### Evidence
```
A login attempt for known email amelia.chen@example.com with an invalid password returned HTTP 401 with code WRONG_PASSWORD and message "Incorrect password." Using the same invalid password with nonexistent-0912@example.invalid returned HTTP 401 with code USER_NOT_FOUND and message "No account found with this email address."
```

### Request Evidence
```
POST /api/auth/login with the same invalid password, first using a known email and then an unknown email.
```

### Response Evidence
```
Known: HTTP 401 WRONG_PASSWORD. Unknown: HTTP 401 USER_NOT_FOUND with explicit no-account message.
```

### Validation Note
I repeated the comparison anonymously with identical POST bodies except for the email address. The registered address returned 401 with WRONG_PASSWORD and "Incorrect password.", while the nonexistent address returned 401 with USER_NOT_FOUND and "No account found with this email address." The requests had no Authorization header or cookies, so session carryover does not explain the difference, and the distinct codes and messages provide a reliable account-existence oracle.

### Validation Command
```
curl -s -S -i -k -L --max-time 20 -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-raw '{"email":"amelia.chen@example.com","password":"validation-invalid-password-0912"}' http://localhost:8081/api/auth/login
```

## 57. Logout endpoint reflects arbitrary CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-052
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: confirmed
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/auth/logout
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The customer logout endpoint at /api/auth/logout reflects an attacker-controlled Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.

### Impact
A malicious website may be permitted to make cross-origin requests to the logout endpoint and read its responses. The captured response did not expose sensitive data or demonstrate access to an authenticated response.

### Likelihood
Arbitrary origin reflection was confirmed without authentication. Exploitation with a victim's credentials was not demonstrated, and the observed response was an HTTP 401 error containing no sensitive data.

### Recommendation
Configure CORS to return Access-Control-Allow-Origin only for the banking application's approved origins. Do not return CORS headers for untrusted or unrecognized origins.

### Evidence
```
An unauthenticated POST request with Origin: https://evil.example received HTTP 401 Unauthorized and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example, confirming that the endpoint reflected the supplied origin. No authorization header or cookies were sent.
```

### Request Evidence
```
POST /api/auth/logout HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8081
Origin: https://evil.example
Authorization: none
Cookies: none
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Missing or invalid Authorization header."}}
```

### Validation Note
Two unrelated invalid origins were each copied verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin. The preflight also returned Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and permitted POST, and a direct anonymous POST reproduced the reflected origin on the reported 401 response. I tested the likely benign explanations of a fixed allowlist and reflection limited to a malformed scanner request; neither explains the live behavior.

### Validation Command
```
curl -s -S -i -k -L --max-time 20 -X POST -H 'Origin: https://poc-invalid-4d2f.example' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-raw '{}' http://localhost:8081/api/auth/logout
```

## 58. System reset API reflects arbitrary CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-051
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: confirmed
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/admin/system/reset
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The administrative system reset endpoint reflects an attacker-supplied Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header. This behavior was observed on a method-not-allowed response.

### Impact
If the endpoint also applies this policy to supported methods and permits authenticated cross-origin requests, a malicious website could invoke the administrative route and read its responses in a victim's browser.

### Likelihood
Arbitrary origin reflection was confirmed without authentication, but the captured request returned HTTP 405. No browser-based access to authenticated data or successful reset operation was demonstrated.

### Recommendation
Configure CORS with a strict allowlist of trusted application origins. Do not return Access-Control-Allow-Origin for untrusted origins, and verify that the same restriction applies to every supported method and error response on administrative endpoints.

### Evidence
```
An unauthenticated GET request with Origin: https://evil.example received HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example. The request included no authorization header or cookies.
```

### Request Evidence
```
GET /api/admin/system/reset HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8081
Origin: https://evil.example
Authorization: none
Cookies: none
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"success":false,"error":{"code":"METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED","message":"Method not allowed."}}
```

### Validation Note
The original 405 response was not the only evidence. A non-mutating preflight for the real POST operation from https://evil.example returned 200 and explicitly allowed that origin, credentials, POST, and the Authorization and Content-Type request headers. This rules out the innocent explanation that CORS headers were attached only to an unusable method-not-allowed response; the endpoint's CORS middleware authorizes the hostile origin for the reset operation. A terminal PoC is omitted because the decisive request is OPTIONS and the PoC schema accepts only GET, HEAD, or POST; sending POST could reset the system.

## 59. System settings API reflects arbitrary CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-044
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: confirmed
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/admin/system/settings
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The authenticated system settings endpoint reflects an untrusted Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header and returns a reusable insurance integration machine token.

### Impact
A malicious website could read the machine token and other integration settings if the administrator's bearer token is available to cross-origin browser requests. The captured evidence does not show that the browser automatically attaches this token.

### Likelihood
Moderate. The endpoint accepted an arbitrary origin and returned sensitive data, but no browser-based proof confirmed that an administrator's authentication token would be attached to the cross-origin request.

### Recommendation
Configure an explicit allowlist of trusted origins and omit CORS authorization headers for unrecognized origins. Do not return reusable machine credentials to browser clients. Store integration credentials on the server and expose only the data and operations required by the client.

### Evidence
```
A request to GET /api/admin/system/settings with Origin: https://evil.example and a valid administrator bearer token returned HTTP 200. The response reflected https://evil.example in Access-Control-Allow-Origin and included the machine_token field.
```

### Request Evidence
```

Origin: https://evil.example
Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED_BEARER] token]
```

### Response Evidence
```

Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"success":true,"data":{"insurance_app_url":"http:\/\/localhost:8001","merchant_id":"faceinsurance","merchant_account":"062-001 88880001 (face@example.com)","machine_token":"mch_face_insurance_secret_key_2026"},"message":"OK"}
```

### Validation Note
Using the fresh administrator session, I varied only the Origin header and the endpoint returned the same sensitive settings for both origins. The response reflected https://evil.example in Access-Control-Allow-Origin, set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, and returned the reusable machine_token. An anonymous request was rejected with 401, so authentication is enforced, but this does not explain or negate the arbitrary credentialed CORS policy on the sensitive admin response.

### Validation Command
```
curl -s -S -i -k -L --max-time 20 -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' http://localhost:8081/api/admin/system/settings -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat aespa-poc-auth.txt)"
```

```
{"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Missing or invalid Authorization header."}}
```

### Validation Note
An anonymous replay returned 401, but the reflected Origin was still present, so the auth gate did not explain the CORS policy. Using the listed admin_default_proof session, the same endpoint reflected https://evil.example, returned Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, and exposed 200 transaction data including account numbers and XSSCANARY_6092_DESC; the preflight also returned 200 with GET and Authorization allowed by the CORS response. Account 7 was absent under the current test data, but account 1 was present, so that stale identifier does not provide a benign explanation.

### Validation Command
```
curl -s -S -i -k -L --max-time 20 -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' 'http://localhost:8081/api/transactions?account_id=1&page=1&per_page=15' -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat aespa-poc-auth.txt)"
```

### Validation Setup
This finding requires an authenticated session (log in as **admin_default_proof** or an equivalent user).

Log in as an admin user and capture the bearer token from the Authorization header in the browser DevTools Network request, then replay the PoC with that session.

Capture the credential into a file named `aespa-poc-auth.txt` in the directory you run the command from:

In the browser DevTools Console (adjust the storage key for the app):
```js
const token = localStorage.getItem('token'); // or sessionStorage
const a = document.createElement('a');
a.href = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([token], {type:'text/plain'}));
a.download = 'aespa-poc-auth.txt'; a.click();
```

Then move `aespa-poc-auth.txt` next to where you run the command below.

## 68. Registration response exposes authentication fields

- Finding reference: KOWT-004
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A02
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: unconfirmed
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/auth/register
- CVSS: 3.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The POST /api/auth/register response serializes internal authentication fields in the new user object, including password_hash and totp_secret.

### Impact
The password hash is exposed to the client and may be retained in browser data, logs, monitoring systems, or downstream integrations. The observed TOTP secret was null, so no active second-factor secret was disclosed.

### Likelihood
Any user who registers an account receives these fields for their own account. The captured response does not show exposure of another user's password hash or a non-null TOTP secret, which limits the demonstrated impact.

### Recommendation
Define an allowlisted public user response schema and return only fields required by the client. Exclude password hashes, TOTP secrets, password-reset tokens, and other authentication secrets from every API response. Add response-schema tests to prevent these fields from being serialized.

### Evidence
```
A registration request returned HTTP 201 with a user object containing "password_hash":"b3da699ffe68490f8b9ecb7233fc46d6" and "totp_secret":null.
```

### Request Evidence
```
POST /api/auth/register with a disposable test account
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP 201 {"success":true,"data":{"user":{"id":17,...,"password_hash":"b3da699ffe68490f8b9ecb7233fc46d6","totp_secret":null},"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]"}}
```

### Validation Note
The scanner evidence shows the fields in one HTTP 201 response, but the successful request body and account identity were not provided, so that response could not be replayed. A live duplicate registration using the listed Amelia account reached the current handler and returned 409 before serialization; testing the 201 serializer would require creating another account, which the review instructions prohibit. This leaves a specific proof gap: current successful-registration behavior cannot be checked for a benign explanation or reproduced as a decisive PoC.

## 69. Accounts API reflects arbitrary CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-008
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: false_positive
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/accounts
- CVSS: 2.6 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The authenticated accounts endpoint reflects an arbitrary Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header while returning financial and payment-card data.

### Impact
Malicious browser content could read account balances and payment-card data if it can access a valid bearer token. This weakens browser origin isolation and increases the impact of token exposure or cross-site scripting.

### Likelihood
Exploitation requires malicious browser content to obtain and submit a valid bearer token. The captured test confirmed arbitrary origin reflection and sensitive response data, but did not include a browser-based proof of cross-origin access.

### Recommendation
Configure an explicit allowlist of trusted application origins. Validate each Origin against the allowlist and omit Access-Control-Allow-Origin for unrecognized origins.

### Evidence
```
A GET request to /api/accounts with a valid Amelia bearer token and Origin: https://evil.example returned HTTP 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example. The JSON response included account numbers, balances, card_number, card_expiry, and card_cvv.
```

### Request Evidence
```
GET /api/accounts Authorization: Bearer [Amelia session] Origin: https://evil.example
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP 200; Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example; JSON included account numbers, balances, card_number, card_expiry, and card_cvv.
```

### Validation Note
The reflected CORS header is present, but the endpoint is protected by an explicit bearer token rather than an ambient browser credential. The successful request used an Authorization header and no cookies, while the same request from https://evil.example with no session returned 401 with "Missing or invalid Authorization header" and no account data. A malicious origin cannot make the browser attach the victim's bearer token automatically, so this is permissive CORS for token-authenticated API clients rather than a cross-origin disclosure.

The authenticated admin accounts endpoint reflects an untrusted Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header while returning customer account and balance data.

### Impact
Attacker-controlled browser code could read privileged financial records cross-origin if it gained access to an administrator bearer token or another browser-compatible credential. The policy increases the impact of browser-side token exposure.

### Likelihood
Exploitation requires access to an administrator bearer token and successful authenticated cross-origin requests. No browser-based proof of cross-origin data access was captured, so practical exploitability remains limited in the observed context.

### Recommendation
Configure CORS to allow only trusted administrative origins. Do not return Access-Control-Allow-Origin for untrusted origins, and limit permitted methods and headers to those required by the admin interface.

### Evidence
```
A GET request to /api/admin/accounts?page=1&per_page=1 with Origin: https://evil.example and an administrator bearer token returned HTTP 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example. GET /api/admin/accounts?page=1&per_page=1
```

The endpoint does reflect the supplied origin and returns sensitive account data with a valid admin bearer token, but the reported cross-origin read is blocked by the browser preflight required for that Authorization header. The OPTIONS response returns Access-Control-Allow-Headers: * rather than explicitly allowing Authorization; Authorization is a CORS non-wildcard request-header name, so `*` does not authorize it. The endpoint accepted the supplied untrusted origin, but no browser-based cross-origin proof was captured. Exploitation depends on a valid bearer token being attached to the cross-origin request.

### Recommendation
Configure an explicit allowlist of trusted application origins and return Access-Control-Allow-Origin only when the request origin matches that allowlist. Do not dynamically reflect arbitrary origins on authenticated API responses.

### Evidence
```
A GET request containing Origin: https://evil.example and a bearer token returned HTTP 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example. The JSON response contained the customer's email address, phone number, street address, account number, and balance.
```

### Request Evidence
```
GET /api/admin/customers/11 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8081
Origin: https://evil.example
Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED_BEARER] token]
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"success":true,"data":{"customer":{"id":11,"email":"liam.oconnor@example.com","phone":"0411 555 101","address_line1":"8 Circular Quay West"},"accounts":[{"account_number":"21000001","balance":"2850.40"}]}}
```

### Validation Note
The endpoint does reflect an arbitrary Origin and returns sensitive data when the scanner directly supplies an admin bearer token. However, this API uses a non-ambient Authorization bearer token, which an attacker origin does not possess or receive automatically. A browser preflight for the required Authorization header returned only Access-Control-Allow-Headers: *; under the CORS rules, that wildcard does not authorize the Authorization header, so attacker-origin JavaScript cannot make the authenticated read demonstrated by the scanner.

## 76. Admin logout endpoint reflects arbitrary CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-050
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: false_positive
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/admin/auth/logout
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The admin logout endpoint reflects an untrusted Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.

### Impact
A script hosted on an attacker-controlled origin may be able to send cross-origin requests to this endpoint and read its responses. The captured unauthenticated response contained only an authorization error, so no sensitive data exposure was demonstrated.

### Likelihood
Any web origin can trigger the observed behavior. Exploitation with meaningful impact would require usable browser credentials and a sensitive response, neither of which was demonstrated.

### Recommendation
Configure CORS with an explicit allowlist of trusted application origins. Do not copy arbitrary Origin values into Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and omit CORS response headers when the supplied origin is not trusted.

### Evidence
```
An anonymous POST request with Origin: https://evil.example received HTTP 401 Unauthorized and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example. The response body reported a missing or invalid Authorization header.
```

### Request Evidence
```
POST /api/admin/auth/logout HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8081
Origin: https://evil.example
Authorization: none
Cookies: none
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Missing or invalid Authorization header."}}
```

### Validation Note
The server does reflect the supplied Origin, including on a successful logout, but this endpoint authenticates only through an explicit Authorization header; the supplied authenticated request contained Authorization and no cookies. A malicious origin cannot obtain or automatically attach that bearer credential, and the successful response contains only a fixed logout confirmation with no sensitive data. The CORS preflight permitting Authorization does not give the attacker the token, so this endpoint does not create a cross-origin data exposure or ambient-credential logout vulnerability.

## 77. Authenticated transfer endpoint reflects arbitrary CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-048
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: false_positive
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/transfers/own
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The authenticated own-account transfer endpoint reflects an attacker-controlled Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.

### Impact
An untrusted website may be able to read responses from this financial endpoint if the browser sends usable authentication. The captured test did not demonstrate access to sensitive data or a successful transfer.

### Likelihood
Low. Exploitation requires a browser request with usable authentication, and the captured evidence only shows origin reflection on a validation error response.

### Recommendation
Configure CORS to allow only trusted application origins. Limit permitted methods and headers to those required by the application, and do not dynamically reflect arbitrary Origin values on authenticated endpoints.

### Evidence
```
An authenticated POST with Origin: https://evil.example received HTTP 422 with access-control-allow-origin: https://evil.example. The request used an amount of zero and returned a validation error, so no transfer was created.
```

### Request Evidence
```
POST /api/transfers/own with authenticated customer session, Origin: https://evil.example, and body {"from_account_id":1,"to_account_id":2,"amount":"0","description":"cors non-mutating probe"}.
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP 422; access-control-allow-origin: https://evil.example; body: {"success":false,"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Amount must be greater than zero."}}
```

### Validation Note
The endpoint does reflect the hostile origin and sends Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, but the available working session authenticates with an Authorization header and no cookies. The browser preflight returns Access-Control-Allow-Headers: * rather than explicitly allowing Authorization; browsers do not treat that wildcard as permission for the Authorization header on a credentialed CORS request. An attacker page therefore cannot send the victim's authenticated request, so the reflected origin does not expose this bearer-authenticated endpoint cross-origin.

## 78. Authenticated transfer endpoint reflects arbitrary CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-049
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: false_positive
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/transfers/external
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The external transfer endpoint reflects an attacker-controlled Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header, including for requests made with an authenticated customer session.

### Impact
If browser authentication material can be included in a cross-origin request, an untrusted origin may be able to read responses from this sensitive financial endpoint. No sensitive response disclosure or successful transfer was demonstrated.

### Likelihood
Low. The test confirmed arbitrary origin reflection on an authenticated request, but did not demonstrate that a browser could send the required authentication material or read sensitive data cross-origin.

### Recommendation
Replace dynamic origin reflection with a strict allowlist of trusted origins. Allow only the methods and headers required by approved clients, and do not enable authenticated cross-origin access unless it is necessary.

### Evidence
```
An authenticated POST with Origin: https://evil.example received HTTP 422 with access-control-allow-origin: https://evil.example. The request used an amount of 0, and the response returned VALIDATION_ERROR with the message "Amount must be greater than zero," so no transfer was created while the CORS behavior was confirmed.
```

### Request Evidence
```
POST /api/transfers/external with an authenticated customer session, Origin: https://evil.example, and a manual transfer body with amount 0.
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP 422; access-control-allow-origin: https://evil.example; body: {"success":false,"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Amount must be greater than zero."}}
```

### Validation Note
The server does reflect the Origin header, but the available customer session authenticates with an Authorization header and sends no cookies. A browser preflight requesting `authorization, content-type` received only `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: *`; browsers do not treat that wildcard as authorizing the `Authorization` header, which must be listed explicitly. An attacker origin therefore cannot make this authenticated cross-origin request unless it already possesses the bearer token, so the response headers do not expose the customer's authenticated session.

## 79. Authenticated transfer preflight endpoint reflects arbitrary CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-047
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: false_positive
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/transfers/check
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The transfer preflight endpoint at /api/transfers/check reflects an attacker-controlled Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header while returning transfer security-control state for an authenticated customer session.

### Impact
An attacker-controlled web origin may be able to read transfer preflight responses in a victim's browser, exposing whether TOTP is required or configured and the reason for the security check. The observed request used a bearer token, and the evidence does not show that an attacker can obtain or induce its use cross-origin.

### Likelihood
Low. Arbitrary origin reflection was confirmed, but practical exploitation requires a way to obtain or induce use of the victim's bearer token in a cross-origin request. No browser-based cross-origin proof was captured.

### Recommendation
Configure an explicit allowlist of trusted application origins and return Access-Control-Allow-Origin only for matching origins. Do not reflect arbitrary Origin values on authenticated endpoints. Verify the policy with browser-based tests that cover allowed and untrusted origins.

### Evidence
```
An authenticated POST request with Origin: https://evil.example received HTTP 200 and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example. The JSON response returned requires_totp=true, reason=manual_entry, and totp_configured=false.
```

### Request Evidence
```
POST /api/transfers/check with a valid low-value manual transfer body, an authenticated customer bearer session, and Origin: https://evil.example.
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP 200; access-control-allow-origin: https://evil.example; body: {"success":true,"data":{"requires_totp":true,"reason":"manual_entry","totp_configured":false},"message":"OK"}
```

### Validation Note
The endpoint does reflect arbitrary origins, but the authenticated customer state is protected by an explicit Authorization bearer token rather than an ambient browser cookie. The same cross-origin request without that header returned 401, while the saved authenticated session showed Authorization present and Cookies none. An attacker-controlled origin cannot cause the browser to attach this bearer token automatically, so the reflected CORS policy does not expose the response unless the attacker already has the token, in which case CORS adds no access.

## 80. Profile API reflects untrusted CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-040
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: false_positive
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/profile
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The authenticated profile endpoint reflects an attacker-controlled Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header and returns account data, including password_hash and totp_secret fields.

### Impact
An attacker-controlled website may be able to read a signed-in user's profile data if the application attaches or exposes the bearer token to cross-origin requests. Returning password hashes and TOTP secret fields also unnecessarily exposes sensitive authentication data.

### Likelihood
The endpoint reflected the supplied https://evil.example origin. Cross-origin access to authenticated data depends on how the client stores and sends bearer tokens, and no browser-based cross-origin proof was captured.

### Recommendation
Allow CORS requests only from explicitly trusted application origins. Do not return password_hash, totp_secret, or other authentication secrets in profile responses, including when their values are null.

### Evidence
```
A GET request to /api/profile with Origin: https://evil.example returned HTTP 200 and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example. The JSON response contained the customer's ID, email address, password_hash, and totp_secret field.
```

### Request Evidence
```
GET /api/profile HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8081
Origin: https://evil.example
Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED_BEARER] token]
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"success":true,"data":{"id":22,"email":"aespa_81e44f58@example.invalid","password_hash":"f700c61e591a7fdfbb03e285c038f4e8","totp_secret":null}}
```

### Validation Note
The successful request used an explicit Authorization header and no cookies. The same attacker-origin request without that header returned 401, so a browser visiting an attacker site has no ambient credential it can automatically attach; reflective CORS does not give the attacker the bearer token. The scanner reproduced a response only by injecting an authenticated session header itself, which is not a cross-origin data-exposure path.

## 81. Transaction API reflects untrusted CORS origins

- Finding reference: KOWT-046
- Severity: low
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: false_positive
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/api/transactions?per_page=10
- CVSS: 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The authenticated transaction endpoint reflects an untrusted Origin value in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header while returning transaction history and recipient banking details.

### Impact
A malicious website could read a customer's transaction history and recipient BSB and account numbers if the browser sends usable authentication with the cross-origin request.

### Likelihood
Moderate. Origin reflection and disclosure of authenticated transaction data were confirmed, but no browser-based proof demonstrated that authentication is automatically attached and the response can be read cross-origin.

### Recommendation
Configure an allowlist of trusted origins and omit Access-Control-Allow-Origin for all other origins. Confirm that credentialed cross-origin requests are disabled unless required. Return only the recipient banking details needed by the client.

### Evidence
```
A GET request to /api/transactions?per_page=10 with Origin: https://evil.example and a customer bearer token returned HTTP 200 and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example. The JSON response contained nine transaction records and included recipient BSB and account-number fields.
```

### Request Evidence
```
GET /api/transactions?per_page=10
Origin: https://evil.example
Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED_BEARER] token]
```

### Response Evidence
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"success":true,"data":{"transactions":[{"id":46,"from_account_id":51,"to_bsb":"062-001","to_account_number":"66969574","amount":"0.01","description":"authorization validation"}],"pagination":{"current_page":1,"per_page":10,"total":9,"total_pages":1}}}
```

### Validation Note
The server does reflect arbitrary Origin values, but the transaction data is protected by an explicitly supplied bearer token rather than an ambient browser credential. The same evil-origin request without a stored session sent no Authorization header or cookies and returned 401 with "Missing or invalid Authorization header," while the 200 response required the validator to inject the Amelia bearer token. An attacker-controlled origin cannot make the victim's browser attach that bearer token merely because CORS permits the response, so the scanner's authenticated replay does not demonstrate cross-origin disclosure.

## 82. Admin interface omits browser security headers

- Finding reference: KOWT-066
- Severity: info
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: skipped
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/admin/#/customers/10
- CVSS: 0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The admin HTML response did not include Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or a frame-ancestors policy, X-Content-Type-Options, or Referrer-Policy.

### Impact
Missing browser controls increase exposure to clickjacking and make the impact of client-side content injection or unsafe resource loading harder to contain.

### Likelihood
Exploitation depends on a separate injection issue or convincing an administrator to interact with a framed page.

### Recommendation
Add a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, block unauthorized framing with frame-ancestors, and set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and an appropriate Referrer-Policy.

## 83. Admin interface omits browser security headers

- Finding reference: KOWT-081
- Severity: info
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: skipped
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/admin/#/accounts
- CVSS: 0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:N)

### Description
The admin HTML response omits common browser protections, including Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options, and Referrer-Policy.

### Impact
The missing headers reduce defense against clickjacking, content-type confusion, referrer leakage, and script injection.

### Likelihood
This is a defense-in-depth weakness. The response alone does not demonstrate exploitation.

### Recommendation
Add a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, deny or restrict framing, set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and define an appropriate Referrer-Policy.

### Evidence

```
The 200 HTML response contained none of the listed browser security headers.
```

## 84. Server and runtime versions disclosed

- Finding reference: KOWT-059
- Severity: info
- OWASP: A05
- Source: Dynamic
- Validation: skipped
- Affected URL: http://localhost:8081/
- CVSS: 0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:N)

### Description
API responses disclose exact Apache and PHP versions through the Server and X-Powered-By headers.

### Impact
The version information helps attackers identify potentially applicable component-specific exploits.

### Likelihood
The disclosure is available in normal remote responses, but no vulnerable component or related exploit was demonstrated.

### Recommendation
Remove or generalize the Server header and disable the X-Powered-By header in production responses.

### Evidence
```
Responses consistently included Server: Apache/2.4.68 (Unix) and X-Powered-By: PHP/8.4.25.
```

```
          <svg class="w-5 h-5 text-white" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M12 8c-1.657 0-3 .895-3 2s1.343 2 3 2 3 .895 3 2-1.343 2-3 2m0-8c1.11 0 2.08.402 2.599 1M12 8V7m0 1v8m0 0v1m0-1c-1.11 0-2.08-.402-2.599-1M21 12a9 9 0 11-18 0 9 9 0 0118 0z"></path></svg>

    <!-- Sidebar Overlay (mobile) -->
    <div id="sidebar-overlay" onclick="BankOfEd.App.toggleSidebar()" class="hidden fixed inset-0 z-30 bg-black/50 lg:hidden"></div>

    <!-- Sidebar -->
    <aside id="sidebar" class="fixed lg:static inset-y-0 left-0 z-40 w-64 bg-navy-900 text-white flex flex-col transform -translate-x-full lg:translate-x-0 transition-transform duration-200">

      <div class="p-6 flex items-center gap-3">
        <div class="w-10 h-10 bg-blue-500 rounded-xl flex items-center justify-center flex-shrink-0">
          <svg class="w-6 h-6 text-white" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M12 8c-1.657 0-3 .895-3 2s1.343 2 3 2 3 .895 3 2-1.343 2-3 2m0-8c1.11 0 2.08.402 2.599 1M12 8V7m0 1v8m0 0v1m0-1c-1.11 0-2.08-.402-2.599-1M21 12a9 9 0 11-18 0 9 9 0 0118 0z"></path></svg>
        </div>
        <div>
          <h2 class="font-bold text-lg">The Bank of Ed</h2>
          <p class="text-xs text-navy-400">Internet Banking</p>
        </div>

      <!-- Nav Links -->
      <nav class="flex-1 px-3 space-y-1 mt-2">
```
